doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Dishwashing in Boston and getting his Schillinger fee back
summary: He fails as a waiter, washes dishes, cannot afford the school and gets his application fee back, hearing a beautiful bowed bass in the building.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: on? That’s not a tux. Out.” So I was out. So anyway I ended up getting a job at Steuben’s Restaurant in Boston as a dishwasher. And I washed a few pots and pans. And I think that lasted a little over a week too. But in the meantime I went back to the Schillinger House and asked for my application fee back. I think it was like $25 or something.

Yeah. He says, “we don’t normally do this.” Probably the dean. But he says, “we understand your situation.” This is where Herb Pomeroy and all those people taught, and John LaPorta and all, they teach up there. And he says, “we don’t normally do this but we understand your situation” so they gave me the money back. And I took the money and applied it toward my room.
Did you decide not to go there because you just couldn’t afford it?
